items.title: Sudhalter interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: And it was very interesting, the lessons with him, because he was very insistent on learning the lyrics to songs before you played them.

ctx.x: Yeah. And I’m trying to think — I know one of the big teachers I had, but this was a little bit later — I’m trying to think who I studied with in Boston because I know there was someone — maybe I’ll think of that later. But I went to Eddie Barefield in New York, he was wonderful. And then I went to Big Nick Nicholas. And I went to him because of the

colors he got out of the tenor, you know, the beautiful nuances and color, and especially when he played like Strayhorn tunes, and I wanted to get an idea about that. And it was very interesting, the lessons with him, because he was very insistent on learning the lyrics to songs before you played them. And I think that’s where the color came from — understanding the meaning of the song in terms of the lyrics.
Boy, he did a lot of session playing I believe — rock & roll and just about everything that came along.
